instructions:
1. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and arms at your sides.
2. Bend the knee and hip to lower into a quarter squat, swinging your arms back.
3. Drive the arms up and explosively extend the leg to jump straight up.
4. Land softly on the same leg, absorbing the impact with a bent knee.
5. Reset your balance, then complete the set and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the ball of the foot, rolling to the heel to absorb force.
2. Keep the knee tracking over the toes, not caving inward.
3. Use your arm swing to add height and control.
4. Brace your core to stay balanced through each jump.
name: Unilateral Jumps

instructions:
1. Set up in a forearm plank with elbows under shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
3. Lift one arm off the floor and reach it forward or tuck it to your side.
4. Resist any rotation, keeping your hips and shoulders square to the floor.
5. Hold for the set time, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and square; do not let them twist toward the lifted side.
2. Widen your feet for a more stable base if needed.
3. Brace as if bracing for a punch to resist rotation.
4. Keep your neck neutral, gaze just ahead of your hands.
name: Unilateral Plank_Female

instructions:
1. Set up in a push-up position with feet wide for balance and one hand on the floor under your chest.
2. Place the free arm behind your back or along your side.
3. Brace your core and resist rotation, keeping hips square.
4. Bend the working elbow to lower your chest toward the floor.
5. Press through the hand to push back up to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Spread your feet wide to create a stable base and reduce twisting.
2. Keep your hips and shoulders square; resist rotating toward the working arm.
3. Keep the working elbow tucked at roughly 45 degrees from the body.
4. Brace the core hard throughout to control the descent.
name: One Arm Push Up_Female

instructions:
1. Stand holding a medicine ball overhead with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Slam the ball hard to the floor, hinging through the hips and bending forward.
3. Place your hands down and jump or step your feet back into a plank.
4. Lower your chest, then push up and jump the feet back to your hands.
5. Pick up the ball and explosively jump up, pressing it overhead.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the slam with your lats and abs, not just your arms.
2. Keep your core braced when jumping back to protect your lower back.
3. Use a non-bouncing slam ball so it does not rebound into your face.
4. Land softly from each jump with bent knees.
name: Med ball slam burpees

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and raise your legs straight toward the ceiling.
2. Hold a medicine ball with both hands, arms extended overhead.
3. Brace your core and crunch your upper back off the floor.
4. Reach the ball up toward your toes at the top of the movement.
5. Lower your shoulders back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by swinging the ball with your arms.
2. Keep your legs as straight and still as possible.
3. Exhale as you crunch up and reach the ball to the toes.
4. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
name: Med ball toe touches
